classification.difficultyReason: With the triangle pairing supplied, derive complementary angles, prove similarity and rearrange a corresponding-side proportion into the stated identity.

content.prompt:
Prove that: The altitude to the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle divides the hypotenuse into two intervals whose product equals the square of the altitude.

Let $AN$ be the altitude to the hypotenuse $BC$ of the right-angled triangle $\triangle ABC$.

spec.description: Triangle ABC has horizontal hypotenuse BC, A above BC, and altitude AN. Right-angle squares mark BAC and ANC. Ordinary source blue linework is rendered black under house style.
spec.mathematics: N lies between B and C; AN is perpendicular to BC; AB is perpendicular to AC. Coordinates construct these relationships without adding numerical givens.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied vertices, altitude and right-angle markers are visible; no proof angles or answers are added.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Prove that $\triangle ABN$ is similar to $\triangle CAN$.

answer.short:
$\triangle ABN\sim\triangle CAN$ (AAA).

Both triangles are right-angled at $N$, and $\angle BAN=\angle ACN$.
answer.worked:
Let $\angle NBA=\alpha$. Since $B,N,C$ are collinear, $\angle ABC=\alpha$.

In the right-angled triangles $ABN$ and $ABC$,
$$\begin{align*}\angle BAN&=90^\circ-\alpha\\\angle ACN&=90^\circ-\alpha.\end{align*}$$
Thus $\angle BAN=\angle ACN$. Also $\angle ANB=\angle CNA=90^\circ$, since $AN\perp BC$.

Therefore $\triangle ABN\sim\triangle CAN$ (AAA).

answer.short:
$AN^2=BN\times CN$.

Use $\dfrac{AN}{CN}=\dfrac{BN}{AN}$ from matching sides of the similar triangles.
answer.worked:
From $\triangle ABN\sim\triangle CAN$, matching sides give
$$\frac{AN}{CN}=\frac{BN}{AN}.$$
Multiplying both sides by $AN\times CN$ gives
$$AN^2=BN\times CN.$$
